chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to Ja'far and Musa: 'And regarding what I have ordered you both, from the witnessing with such and such, is a safety for you both in your Hereafter, and the enforcement of what your parents bequeathed, and righteousness from you both to them, and beware that you do not replace their bequest, nor change it from its state, because they both have exited from that, may Allah be Pleased with them, and that has become a burden upon your necks.'

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has said in His Book regarding the bequest: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin of it is only upon those who alter it; surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing.'

key_terms.الْإِشْهَادِ: Witnessing (attesting to a document or event)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on altering a parent's bequest according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the binding nature of parental bequests in Shia jurisprudence, framing their enforcement as a means of spiritual salvation and filial piety. Imam Abu Ja'far (AS) warns that altering the will transfers the sin onto the heirs, emphasizing that the parents' final wishes remain a debt upon their children's souls. The citation of Surah Al-Baqarah underscores the divine witness to the preservation of testamentary integrity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> wrote to Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Musa<sup>asws</sup>: ‘And with regards to what I<sup>asws</sup> am ordering both of you<sup>asws</sup>, from the (appointment of) witnessed with such and such, is a safety for you<sup>asws</sup> in your<sup>asws</sup> Hereafter, and the enforcement of what I<sup>asws</sup>, your<sup>asws</sup> father, am bequeathing with, and your<sup>asws</sup> righteousness from you<sup>asws</sup> to both of them<sup>asws</sup> (parents), and cautioning that you<sup>asws</sup> do not replace their<sup>asws</sup> bequest, nor change it from its state, because they<sup>asws</sup> both would have exited from that, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased from them<sup>asws</sup>, and that has come to be upon your<sup>asws</sup> necks.

And Allahazwj Blessed and High has Said in Hisazwj Book with regards to the bequest [2:181] So the one who alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it then is only upon the one who alters it; surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, Alayhi al-Salam, wrote to Ja‘far and Musa, this instruction. ‘In the matter of my commanding you to appoint witnesses to so and so issues; it is because it is for your safety and protection in the next world in matters of executing the will, as it requires, that your parents have made to you and your being kind to your parents. You must remain prudent. You must not change their will and alter it from its original condition because they are no more. May Allah be happy with them. It, however, has remained on your shoulder.
Allah, most Blessed, most High, has said in His book, “Whoever intentionally changes the will of a deceased person, he has committed a sin. Allah is All-hearing and All-knowing.” [2:181]’”
